title: Planet DDS enters Canada through Canadian Dental Services partnership
html:
Dental Tribune International

Mon. 23. November 2026

share save

TORONTO, Canada: Canadian Dental Services Corp. (CDS), a Toronto-based dental support organisation that operates dental practices across Canada, has selected Denticon, the practice management software of US dental technology company Planet DDS,  to support clinics in its general dentistry division. The agreement marks Planet DDS’s entry into Canada and brings together CDS’s ambitions to support dentists and clinic growth with Planet DDS’s enterprise platform that connects practice management and other operational data across multiple dental practices.

CDS was founded in 2016 with the aim of improving how dentistry is delivered in Canada, and the company is now working with Planet DDS to set the standard for how Canadian dental support organisations operate. CDS is transitioning participating clinics from more than six existing practice management systems to Denticon, which forms part of Planet DDS’s cloud-based DentalOS platform. The platform connects operations through a shared data foundation and can be extended through add-on suites such as Clinical Voice+, Imaging+, Patient+ and Payments+, which support clinical documentation, imaging, patient engagement and payment processing.

“We built CDS to take the management burden off dentists so they can focus on their patients,” said Jeremy D. Behar, founder and CEO of CDS. “Moving our clinics onto one platform gives every one of our amazing clinic teams, along with our clinic support centre and our call centre, the same view of the business. This then moves our network further into operational centralisation that is meant to make delivering great dental care and shopping for great dental care more seamless and more efficient across our national footprint.”

A shared data foundation for clinic growth

By moving participating clinics to Denticon, CDS aims to standardise reporting, simplify infrastructure management and give its call centre a common view of clinic operations. That shared foundation is designed to reduce process debt—the additional steps and workarounds that can accumulate as an organisation grows—and help CDS manage performance and support continued clinic growth.

“Jeremy and the CDS team are building what Canadian dentistry needs: a friction-reduced, connected organisation where growth doesn’t mean adding another disconnected system,” said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. “We’re proud to be the enterprise platform behind that vision, and we’re ready to support more Canadian dental groups as they follow CDS’s lead.”

The first step in a broader Canada strategy

The CDS partnership lays the foundation for Planet DDS’s broader strategy for expansion across Canada. The company intends to bring the same model to other Canadian dental groups: shared data, centralised visibility and cloud-native infrastructure designed to support growth without multiplying disconnected systems. More information about Planet DDS is available on the company’s website.
